jobs.title: Everything in the car
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 19, thin young man with a slouch, three days' stubble, dark hair grown longer. WOOD usually wears brown canvas chore coat with a frayed cuff and one mismatched button, hands in its pockets, plain tee, dark jeans. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Wednesday, week two. A classmate asks what's in the box on the Datsun's back seat. 'Everything.' The novel rides to Newport every day and never comes in. Panel 1: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, a rusted small car in a college lot with a taped cardboard box on its back seat, a classmate peering in the window, a young man getting out (in this panel: WOOD). Classmate says "What's in the box?". Wood says "Everything.". Panel 2: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, close-up through a car window of a cardboard box of manuscript pages held by a rubber band, a title on the top page unreadable. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 3: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, a young man locking a car door twice while a classmate loses interest (in this panel: WOOD). Classmate says "...Cool.". Wood says "It's not. It's just everything.". Panel 4: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, a young man walking away from a locked rusted car in a lot with a cardboard box visible on its back seat, no words (in this panel: WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23; @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17.
